findings.title: Stale folder-tree cache is reused after the DB requery, so the new denial is cached wrongly
findings.body: When cached permissions don't allow the request, `Check` requeries permissions from the DB and calls `checkPermission` again. For resources with folder support, that call goes through `checkInheritedPermissions` and `buildFolderTree`, which reads `folderCache` with its 30s TTL. Only the permission map is refreshed. If a user creates a child folder under a parent they have inherited access to, the cached tree doesn't contain the new folder. The check fails again and the result is stored in `permDenialCache` for another 30s. That is the same "can't access what I just created" bug this PR targets, now sticky for nested folders and for dashboards inside them. The fallback should also bypass or refresh the folder cache, or the denial should not be cached when the tree may be stale.

findings.title: Denial cache can hide a resource that becomes accessible right after a denied check
findings.body: Every denial is cached for 30s under (namespace, user, action, name, parent). Any check issued before the permission exists is remembered as a denial. Examples are an existence or read probe before creation completes, or a permission granted moments after a check. Subsequent checks short-circuit and never reach the DB requery that this PR adds. So the newly created dashboard or folder can still be inaccessible for up to 30s. The denial entry is not invalidated when permissions are refreshed or changed.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and shares the `perm_` prefix with the permission cache
findings.body: The key is `ns.perm_<uid>_<action>_<name>_<parent>`, built by plain concatenation with `_` and sharing the same underlying cache and the `perm_` prefix with `userPermCacheKey`. Names or UIDs containing `_` can make distinct tuples map to the same key. For example, name `a_b` with parent `c` collides with name `a` and parent `b_c`. The key can also overlap with `userPermCacheKey` for a user whose UID contains underscores. A collision would wrongly deny an unrelated resource. The key should use a distinct prefix such as `perm_denial_` and an unambiguous separator or encoding.

findings.title: No test that a DB-confirmed denial is written to the denial cache
findings.body: `TestService_CacheCheck` only pre-populates `permDenialCache` and checks that it is honored. Nothing verifies the write path, where a deny from the DB fallback populates the denial cache. Nothing verifies that the DB is not hit again on a repeat check. Nothing covers the anonymous or render identity paths through the new `getCachedIdentityPermissions`, or the folder-inheritance fallback. The `Check`-level tests also never assert how many DB calls the fallback makes.

findings.title: `TestService_getUserPermissions` still has a dead `cacheHit` branch after the cached case was removed
findings.body: The cache-hit test case was deleted because `getUserPermissions` no longer reads the cache. The `cacheHit` field and the branches that set the cache and expect `store.calls == 1` are now unreachable. They are misleading leftovers, and the new cache-first behavior now lives only in `Check` and `List`.
